html:
The report of Argentina's National Commission on the Disappearance of Persons (CONADEP), handed to President Raúl Alfonsín in September 1984. Its title, Nunca Más, means "Never Again".

Under the military dictatorship of 1976 to 1983, during the Dirty War, security forces seized thousands of people they called subversives: students, unionists, activists and others. Most were taken to secret detention centres, tortured and killed, and their bodies hidden, often dropped from planes into the sea. They became the "disappeared". Their mothers marched every week in the Plaza de Mayo to demand answers.

When democracy returned in Argentina in 1983, Alfonsín created the commission, led by the writer Ernesto Sabato. It gathered thousands of testimonies, documented about 8,900 disappeared and some 340 secret centres. The report became a bestseller. It was used in the 1985 Trial of the Juntas, which convicted top military leaders, and became a model for truth commissions elsewhere, including after the dictatorship in Chile.
sum: The report of Argentina's National Commission on the Disappearance of Persons (CONADEP), handed to President Raúl Alfonsín in September 1984. Its title, Nunca Más, means "Never Again".
